answer: Sensor-anchored identity — 1,000 fakes cost 1,000 chips: each agent's identity is anchored to one tamper-evident hardware chip that signs its GPS fix and clock. A mesa-top relay cross-checks each reading against the known dune field; a reading whose fix and clock disagree is rejected outright. A software-only farm fails the check before it can answer, so each fake needs a real chip and a real field trip.
